title: The Raft Consensus Algorithm
text: Raft is a consensus algorithm designed as an alternative to Paxos. It was designed to be more understandable than Paxos by means of separation of logic. Raft decomposes consensus into three independent subproblems: leader election, log replication, and safety. A Raft cluster contains several servers, typically five, which allows the system to tolerate two failures. At any given time, each server is in one of three states: leader, follower, or candidate.

title: Quantum Teleportation Mechanics
text: Quantum teleportation is a technique for transferring quantum information from a sender to a receiver situated at an arbitrary distance. First proposed by Charles Bennett and collaborators in 1993, quantum teleportation requires an entangled quantum state shared between sender and receiver. The process does not transfer energy or matter physically. Instead, classical communication channels transmit measurement results, ensuring that quantum teleportation cannot transfer information faster than the speed of light.

title: CRISPR-Cas9 Genome Editing
text: CRISPR-Cas9 is an RNA-guided targeted genome editing technology adapted from bacterial adaptive immune systems. The Cas9 endonuclease forms a ribonucleoprotein complex with synthetic single guide RNA. Upon binding to complementary genomic DNA containing a protospacer adjacent motif, Cas9 induces double-strand breaks. These breaks are subsequently repaired through non-homologous end joining or homology-directed repair, enabling precise genetic modifications.

title: Transformer Attention Mechanisms
text: The Transformer architecture was introduced in the 2017 paper Attention Is All You Need by Vaswani et al. Transformers discard recurrent loops entirely in favor of multi-head self-attention mechanisms. Self-attention enables modeling dependencies between all positions in a sequence simultaneously without sequential recurrence bottleneck. Multi-head attention projects queries, keys, and values into multiple representation subspaces, enhancing representation capability across diverse context scales.

title: NASA 2015 Announcement on Mars Water
text: In September 2015, NASA scientists announced evidence of active liquid water on contemporary Mars. Spectral analysis from the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter detected hydrated perchlorate salts inside recurring slope lineae on warm crater slopes, confirming that these dark recurring flows represent seasonal briny liquid water seeps.

title: USGS 2017 Geological Reassessment of Mars
text: In November 2017, a comprehensive geological survey published by the USGS demonstrated that recurring slope lineae on Mars are dry granular flows rather than flowing liquid water. High-resolution topographical models showed that the streaks terminate at angles matching the angle of repose for loose sand and gravel, disproving liquid water as the primary mechanism.
